query: For multiprincipal-element alloys intended for sustained use in harsh high-temperature environments, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs oxidation resistance and material integrity, and why? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the range over which the hypothesis should hold, relevant supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Formation of a continuous, dense α-Al2O3 scale governs oxidation resistance and preserves material integrity in CoCrFeMnNi-based multiprincipal-element alloys at 900–1200 °C by impeding further oxygen ingress and substrate degradation.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy, solution-annealed and mechanically polished.
generation.intervention: Alloying the baseline HEA with 5–10 at% Al (substituting equally from Co/Fe/Mn/Cr/Ni) to promote selective Al oxidation.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in static air at 900 °C, 1000 °C and 1200 °C for durations up to 1000 h.
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous, low-porosity α-Al2O3 scale of 1–5 µm thickness at the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Preferential oxidation of added Al forms a continuous α-Al2O3 barrier layer that dramatically reduces oxygen diffusion into the substrate and suppresses formation of non-protective mixed oxides.
generation.predicted_outcome: Al-bearing HEA exhibits <50 % of the weight gain of the baseline; oxide layer is dominated by α-Al2O3; substrate shows minimal internal oxidation or grain-boundary attack.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi without Al forms mixed Cr/Mn/Ni oxides, displays high weight gain and pronounced internal oxidation under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: Holds for Al additions up to ~15 at% and temperatures between 900 °C and 1200 °C; at Al > 15 at% or T > 1200 °C scale spallation or embrittlement may occur.
generation.uncertainty: High—direct long-term evidence for continuous α-Al2O3 scale formation in HEA systems is limited.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce baseline and 5 at% Al-alloy specimens with identical processing. Expose both to 1000 °C static air for 500 h. Characterize oxide scales by XRD and SEM/EDS. Measure weight gain and cross-sectional internal oxidation depth.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-alloy specimen shows ≥90 % of the weight gain of the baseline and no continuous α-Al2O3 scale is observed, the hypothesis is falsified.
